docs.title: Welcome to Constructra
docs.text:
This mod is still in development!

Do not expect an official public release any time soon, and especially not a stable one. The info on this page and the rest of the documentation may be inaccurate, unfinished or subject to change.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Constructra tries to be a totally new take on tech mods. Want to create spaghetti belt systems? Go ahead, if it works, it works, and bonus points if it's more efficient too. Wanna absolutely deforest your entire world ending the life of circa 274 organisms to make space for your next big bio nuclear cluster bomb factory? Go. Ahead.

All jokes - which corporate has forced me to call them - aside, you can create almost anything to achieve your goal in some way or another. This mod aims to add a more streamlined game flow of building your future. No more loose ends, just a straight to the point storyline that will force you to expand in only one direction, with optional alternatives of course, but it all ends up the same.

In the last blog I told you to go look at my personal post somewhere else, but tbh that site is kind of shitty, so just have it here in a quote:

The Post

Today I took a quick gander at Material for MkDocs, and decided that THIS was gonna be the way I'm going to make my documentation sites from now on, starting with Constructra!

Did it take me an entire day's worth of time? YES Was it definitely worth it in the end? ALSO YES!!!!

I started by just looking at this simple tutorial made by James Willett, many thanks go to him for creating a Written Guide For The Video that I was able to snoop some bits of code from, I highly suggest looking at his video(s) if you're also just getting started with MkDocs and want to host the site fully for free using GitHub Pages! - The Video - The Guide

Thanks to the many resources it provides, and to the fact it's an easy-to-use program, MkDocs has been a major help in me creating neat and fluid sites, therefore we ignore that this site is busted and runs on some weird Jekyll software that I have no idea of on how it works.

What did I learn today? I'm a dimwit, I've been using Anaconda for ages to setup virtual environments for Python coding and apparently Python has that built in like what?? You can apparently run python -m venv venv and it'll create a fully new environment for yours to use! And you can even make use of it in your terminal by simply running some activate script found in the folders it creates. Wicked!!

For those who are interested in looking at my new baby docs site, I made a docs hub at docs.tiazzz.me, it currently only contains links to Constructra's docs, of course, but when I do decide to add more documentations for my projects, it'll be of great use.

Another reason as to why I made the hud, is so I can get proper DNS set up. Because see, using custom domains with GitHub pages is a pain in the ass. If I want to make a docs site at, let's say, docs.tiazzz.me/site1, and run it in a repo, it'll be tywrap-studios.github.io/site1, now when I link the domain up to it, it'll actually just use the bare docs.tiazzz.me domain, meaning site1 is directly available on docs.tiazzz.me EVEN THOUGH THE CNAME RECORD I HAVE POINTS docs.tiazzz.me TO THE BARE tywrap-studios.github.io DOMAIN!! Now luckily, making a Tywrap-Studios/Tywrap-Studios.github.io repo and putting a CNAME in there has fixed this, because docs.tiazzz.me now routes to that, which means that if I make a repo called Site2, its GitHub pages site would be at tywrap-studios.github.io/Site2, and now I can finally make docs.tiazzz.me/Site2 actually be that.

Here's a small preview for those who don't trust my links: DOESN'T WORK ON MKDOCS CUZ YK

Phew, what a job. Anyway, have a nice day! You can view the sites here (and go back if my post layout thing worked properly lol): - Docs Hub - WIP Constructra Docs

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Status

This mod is not yet stable enough to fully support addons. It is suggested to wait for a full release.

Note

Some parts of the API need resources from outside its package, you will need the bare content mod in order to make it properly function.

Hello fellow developer, welcome to Constructra!

In order to make an addon at this moment, you will have to do a lot of stuff manually, as the mod and its sources are not yet officially released.

docs.title: Maven (Recommended)
docs.text:
You can get the Constructra sources from the jitpack maven repository.

Groovy build.gradle
repositories {
    maven { url = 'https://jitpack.io' }
}

dependencies {
    ...

    // Constructra
    modImplementation "com.github.Tywrap-Studios:Constructra:${project.constructra_version}"
}

docs.title: Local files
docs.text:
Firstly, obtain a constructra-<version>-sources.jar from any of the following sources:

PlatformBuildingGitHub Actions

Currently, Constructra is not publicly downloadable on any mod hosting platform, or on GitHub releases, so you will have to get it manually yourself.

You can do this by cloning the repository and running ./gradlew build in the root directory of the project. Your sources jar will be in a folder called build/libs.

  1. On the main page of the Repository, click "Actions" in the navigation bar on top.
  2. On the left hand side, there is a list of Workflows , click the one named build.
  3. Click into the top NON-FAILED action.
    1. You may filter by branch or release tag using the filters on the right side, or target a specific build in the list. This may be handy if you don't want to end up with an in-dev, unstable or broken version.
  4. Scroll down until you see a text named "Artifacts", after you click this a zip file containing the main jar and the sources jar will be downloaded onto your machine. Extract these jars and use the one that is affixed with -sources.jar.

After obtaining said file, it is best to make a new directory in your project called libs/, and put the jar inside of it.

Now you can manually add it to your repositories and dependencies:

Groovy build.gradle
dependencies {
    ...

    // Constructra
    modImplementation files("libs/constructra-${project.constructra_version}-sources.jar")
}

docs.title: Finalizing
docs.text:
Finally, add the following to your gradle.properties file: 

constructra_version=x.y.z
And replace x.y.z with your major, minor and patch version, e.g. 1.0.0.

When using JitPack

As the repository doesn't have any releases, you can't use release tags, instead, go to the JitPack page and look at how you can instead import a branch. JitPack might not have made an Artifact yet, before trying to use it, if you can properly import the branch by looking at the build status.

Tip: Local versioning

If you are using a local jar, check if the version in the file name corresponds with the version you're trying to use.

  1. Integrated Development Environment, like IntelliJ IDEA or Eclipse. ↩

docs.text: This is a root command and does nothing. When run will throw a syntax error.

docs.title: /constructra nodes flush
docs.text:
Permissions

This command needs permission level 4 or higher by default. This can be configured.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Flushes all the ResourceNodes from the network, no exceptions.

Danger

This is a dangerous command, it can break your progression!

docs.title: /constructra nodes purge
docs.text:
Permissions

This command needs permission level 4 or higher by default. This can be configured.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Purges (removes) all ResourceNodes from the world and the network according to the parameters given. It will spit the removed Nodes and their positions into chat, shared to other ops.

Danger

This is a dangerous command, it can break your progression!

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• pos: The position where the centre of the search should be.
  • range: The range from the centre (pos) of the search.
  • destroy_blocks: Whether to also destroy any of the blocks that the Node contained.

docs.title: /constructra nodes spawn
docs.text:
Permissions

This command needs permission level 2 or higher by default. This can be configured.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Spawns a new ResourceNode in the world and adds it to the network, particularly handy if you accidentally broke a Node or if your natural generation turned out .

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• pos: The position at which to place the centre of the Node.
  • type: What the Resource of the Node should be, the format is namespace:path as it's registry driven.
  • obstructed: Whether the Node should be obstructed (true) or not (false).

docs.title: /constructra reload
docs.text:
Permissions

This command needs permission level 2 or higher by default. This can be configured.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Reloads the server-side config (/run/config/constructra-server.json5), some changes may not be applied, and instead need a full server restart.

docs.title: /constructra
docs.text:
This command has an alias: "/ca"

This alias is configurable!

This command is a root command

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Upon running, will paste the following to chat (generally localized, this is en_us):

Message

Hello $USERNAME! Welcome to Constructra, a mod centred around the creation of machines, tools and automation. You can access the commands by using /constructra, /ca is a shorthand route! If you don't know where to start, feel free to generate yourself either a codex item or press the keybind button to open the codex menu! Have a good day! Nexatek, Build the Future, One Bolt at a Time.

docs.title: Configuring Constructra
docs.text:
If you happen to be stuck, or don't like a particular part of the gameplay, you are probably happy to hear this mod is highly configurable!

There are two types of config files:

  • Server Side
  • Client Side

Both of these files can be found in the run/config directory, and are json5 files, meaning they support comments, which aim to be as informative as possible

Info

Changes on either end will only affect that end, meaning that a changed made on the server won't affect the client side configs, and vice versa.

docs.title: Live examples:
docs.text:
If you want a live example of the configs being used, take a gander at the dev environment configurations!

ClientServer constructra-client.json5
{
    /* (1)
       This file has all the configuration options for Constructra on the client side.
       Changes here will not affect a dedicated server (nor other players online)!

       The following value is irrelevant, do not change it, though.
    */
    "run_info": "None",
    /* The Unit System to use for Measurements.
       Choices: METRIC, FREEDOM
       Type: String (from set)
       Default: METRIC
    */
    "measure_units": "METRIC",
    // Config related to your Play Time Safety.
    "play_time_safety": {
        /* Whether to send 2020 reminders.
           After 20 minutes of playing, look away for 20 seconds.
           Type: Boolean
           Default: false
        */
        "send_2020_reminders": false,
        /* The amount of minutes between 2020 reminders.
           Only applies if send_2020_reminders is true.
           Type: Integer
           Range: >0-60
           Default: 20
        */
        "interval": 20,
        /* Whether to send reminders to take small breaks after long whiles of playing.
           Type: Boolean
           Default: false
        */
        "send_break_reminders": false
    }
}
constructra-server.json5
{
    /* (2)
       This file has all the configuration options for Constructra.
       Do not change the config_version unless you know what you're doing or else some of your changes may be arbitrarily reset and we will use the default values.
    */
    "config_version": "1.0",
    // Config related to Resources.
    "resources": {
        /* The default purity of each Resource in your world.
           Choices: NONE, IMPURE, NORMAL, PURE or RANDOM.
           Type: String (from Set)
           Default: RANDOM
        */
        "default_resource_purity": "RANDOM",
        /* Whether Nodes can be obstructed. When set to false, Nodes don't need to be destructed first in order to be harvested from.
           Type: Boolean
           Default: true
        */
        "do_obstructions": true,
        /* The amount of times you have to consecutively harvest from a Node to be able to de-obstruct it.
           Only applies if do_obstructions is true.
           Type: Integer
           Default: 3
        */
        "consecutive_harvests_for_destruction": 3,
        // Certain Modifiers for ResourceNode Purity Related Mechanics.
        "purity_modifiers": {
            /* Whether the Purity of a ResourceNode affects at which rate the resource is given.
               If false is chosen, we will use the rate of a NORMAL node, so feel free to tweak that value.
               ResourceNodes will still have their Purity displayed!
               Type: Boolean
               Default: true
            */
            "does_purity_affect_rate": true,
            /* The Rate at which a PURE node should give its Resource.
               Type: Double (in seconds)
               Default: 0.8
            */
            "pure": 0.8,
            /* The Rate at which a NORMAL node should give its Resource.
               Type: Double (in seconds)
               Default: 1.2
            */
            "normal": 1.2,
            /* The Rate at which an IMPURE node should give its Resource.
               Type: Double (in seconds)
               Default: 1.9
            */
            "impure": 1.9
        },
        /* Whether to display certain visual hints as to what block is the exact ResourceNode Centre. e.g. through the use of particles.
           Type: Boolean
           Default: false
        */
        "visualize_centres": true
    },
    // Config related to Commands.
    "commands": {
        /* The command alias for the Constructra command. Change this if you're having compatibility issues with other mods.
           Type: String
           Default: ca
        */
        "command_alias": "ca",
        /* The permission level required to use the Node commands in general.
           Type: Integer
           Default: 2
        */
        "perm_lvl_nodes": 2,
        /* The permission level required to remove Nodes from the world. (Both nodes flush and nodes purge.)
           Note that this is a dangerous permission to give as it can break the entire world!
           Type: Integer
           Default: 4
        */
        "perm_lvl_nodes_removal": 4,
        /* The permission level required to reload the Constructra config.
           Type: Integer
           Default: 2
        */
        "perm_lvl_reload": 2
    },
    // Several configurations for utility features.
    "util_config": {
        // Whether to display debug information in the console.
        "debug_mode": true,
        // Whether to suppress all warnings from this mod. NOT RECOMMENDED.
        "suppress_warns": false
    }
}
  1. Click to View extensive info about this Config.
  2. Click to View extensive info about this Config.

docs.title: Client Config
docs.text:
Reference Sheet
  1. Type from Set [choice 1, choice 2,...]
  2. Type in Range, followed by an equation. The variable v is the value to set.

docs.title: "value_name": <default_value>
docs.text:
• Use: Explains use case.
  • Type: States of what JSON Element Type this value is.
    • May specify a Set (1) or a Range (2).
  • Predicate: If this value requires something else to function, it'll be stated here.
  • Default: <default_value>.

docs.title: "run_info": "None"
docs.text:
• Use: This value is irrelevant, and shouldn't/won't be changed by the user.
  • Type: String
  • Default: "None"

docs.title: "measure_units": "METRIC"
docs.text:
• Use: Changes what unit system the mod will use to display measurements for the client.
  • Type: String from Set: [METRIC, FREEDOM]
  • Default "METRIC"

docs.title: "send_2020_reminders": false
docs.text:
• Use: According to research, looking about 6 metres (20 feet) away from your screen for 20 seconds after looking at it for 20+ minutes can improve eyesight and eye performance. Enabling this setting sends you a reminder to look away for 20 seconds using in game toasts.
  • Type: Boolean
  • Default: false

docs.title: "interval": 20
docs.text:
• Use: Defines the interval at which "send_2020_reminders" will be sent. It is recommended to keep this at the default value or lower.
  • Type: Integer in Range: 0<v<=60
  • Predicate: "send_2020_reminders" must be true
  • Default: 20

docs.title: "send_break_reminders": false
docs.text:
• Use: Similar to "send_2020_reminders", although now it sends toasts warning you about your concurrent playtime, hinting you to take a small break.
  • Type: Boolean
  • Default: false

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
To install Constructra, you need to have Fabric Loader installed. You can download it from here. On said page, there is also a download link to the Fabric API, which is also required for Constructra to run.

At the moment, another API install is needed, Fabric Language Kotlin. BlossomBridge, an API we extensively use, is coded in Kotlin as per 2.0.0+. While BlossomBridge itself is bundled with the Constructra jar, the Kotlin adapter is not. You should get it manually here on Modrinth or here on CurseForge .

docs.title: Getting a Mod Jar file
docs.text:
DownloadingBuildingGitHub Actions

Currently, Constructra is not publicly downloadable on any mod hosting platform, or on GitHub releases, so you will have to get it manually yourself.

You can manually build the mod's jar by cloning the repository and running ./gradlew build in the root directory of the project. Your jar will be in a folder called build/libs

Warning

If you're unfamiliar with Gradle and how to build jars manually, check out the other options.

  1. On the main page of the Repository, click "Actions" in the navigation bar on top.
  2. On the left hand side, there is a list of Workflows , click the one named build.
  3. Click into the top NON-FAILED action.
    1. You may filter by branch or release tag using the filters on the right side, or target a specific build in the list. This may be handy if you don't want to end up with an in-dev, unstable or broken version.
  4. Scroll down until you see a text named "Artifacts", after you click this a zip file containing the main jar and the sources jar will be downloaded onto your machine. Extract these jars and use the one that is not affixed with -sources.jar.

docs.title: Finalizing
docs.text: After you've properly downloaded and setup Fabric Loader, input all the jars into your mods folder, and start the game.
